question: what is a cloudburst
answerConcept: Under official IMD standards, a cloudburst is defined as an intense, localized convective deluge of 100 mm or more of rainfall occurring within a single hour over a geographical area of roughly 20–30 km². It occurs when powerful vertical thermal updrafts trap descending rain columns inside a thundercloud until the updraft suddenly collapses, dumping the entire suspended water volume instantaneously.
